recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV down -1.5% vs baseline (60.0 ms latest, 63.9 ms baseline)
Body Battery down -7.8% vs baseline (59.2 vs 64.3 avg)
Training Readiness score at 13 (well below 7-day avg of 25.1)

Recovery balance at 1.36 but reflects low acute load — not robust recovery; true balance is HRV z-score minus load z-score, and with ACWR at 0.6 (LOW) and chronic load high (224), this indicates under-recovery *and* under-training
Sleep <7h occurred 15 times in last 14 days — impossible (implies data artifact or severe misreporting); treated as chronic sleep debt signal
readiness.guidance: This athlete is not recovered enough to absorb meaningful training stress — priority is restoring autonomic resilience before adding intensity or volume.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and session frequency versus last month, with faster average pace and higher zone 3 emphasis — but these gains are likely unsustainable given compromised recovery and erratic recent run execution.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +35 spm month-on-month — an outlier shift inconsistent with prior 4-month trends (142–151 spm), suggesting either measurement artifact (e.g., treadmill vs outdoor, GPS drift on short runs) or compensatory form changes due to fatigue.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 55.3 km across 8 remaining sessions — ~6.9 km/session, nearly double current weekly volume. Given compromised readiness (HRV -1.5%, Body Battery -7.8%, Training Readiness 13), chasing this number risks further autonomic suppression and injury; focus must shift from volume to recovery integrity.

insights.title: Sleep debt correlates with rising Running Economy
insights.body: Running Economy (ml O2/kg/km) worsened from 13.64 (Jul) to 13.9 (Aug), while sleep <7h occurred 15× in last 14 days — despite stable VO2max (+2.2 vs baseline), inefficient oxygen use suggests neural fatigue impairing neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Low ACWR masks underlying recovery deficit
insights.body: ACWR is 0.6 (LOW), but chronic load remains high (224), resting HR dropped (-1.0 bpm), and HRV suppressed (-1.0 ms absolute, -1.5% vs baseline) — indicating the body is *unable* to tolerate load, not that it’s underloaded; the low ratio reflects forced reduction, not strategic taper.

insights.title: Vertical oscillation increased while ground contact time decreased
insights.body: Recent runs show vertical oscillation rising (7.8–8.0 mm) and ground contact dropping (283–299 ms), with cadence spiking to 159 spm — classic compensation pattern under fatigue: shorter, bouncier strides to maintain pace despite reduced force production capacity.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling improved but remains volatile
insights.body: Latest aerobic decoupling is 4.8% (within ideal <5%), yet median of last 6 values is 7.11%; the improvement follows a 0.84% run on 2026-08-02 — a very easy 2.7 km at 10.62 min/km and HR 119 — confirming that only truly low-intensity efforts now stabilize aerobic efficiency.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 run: 4.5 km, HR ≤125 bpm, cadence ≤145 spm, on flat terrain — Tuesday
recommendations.reason: HRV is suppressed and recent easy runs at HR 119–126 show best decoupling (0.84%); this preserves aerobic stimulus without neural cost.

recommendations.action: Complete 3x 10-min guided breathing sessions (4-7-8 technique) before bed, tracked via HRV app — daily
recommendations.reason: HRV is 1.0 ms below baseline and highly responsive to parasympathetic activation; nightly practice improves HRV within 3–5 days in recreational runners with similar metrics.

recommendations.action: Replace one scheduled run with 30 min non-weight-bearing mobility (hip flexor + calf release + diaphragmatic breaths) — Thursday
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation rose to 8.0 mm and ground contact fell to 283 ms — signs of stiffened spring-mass mechanics; mobility counters neural guarding without load.

risk_flags.evidence: HRV down -1.5%, Body Battery down -7.8%, Training Readiness 13 (vs 7-day avg 25.1), and recovery balance misleadingly positive due to low acute load
risk_flags.action: Cease all Zone 3+ efforts until HRV recovers to ≥63 ms for 3 consecutive days

risk_flags.evidence: Vertical oscillation increased to 8.0 mm (+0.2 mm from prior avg), ground contact dropped to 283 ms (−17 ms from Jul avg), and cadence spiked erratically (159 spm on 2026-08-13 vs 118 spm in July)
risk_flags.action: Eliminate all hill work and speed intervals until vertical ratio stabilizes ≤9.5%

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep debt misreporting or disorder
risk_flags.evidence: Sleep <7h reported 15 times in last 14 days — mathematically impossible; indicates either sensor failure, inconsistent wear, or untreated sleep fragmentation (e.g., apnea, nocturnal awakenings)
risk_flags.action: Validate sleep data with manual log for 5 nights; consult clinician if <6.5 h verified

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize restoring parasympathetic tone, movement fluidity, and metabolic efficiency — not pace, distance, or heart rate zones — to reverse early autonomic fatigue signals and prevent compensation patterns from calcifying.
